title: On a Closed-Form Solution of the Brock–Mirman Model with a Finite Horizon: A Shadow-Value Interpretation
affiliations: Meiji University - School of Political Science and Economics

detail.title: On a Closed-Form Solution of the Brock–Mirman Model with a Finite Horizon: A Shadow-Value Interpretation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no relevant financial or non-financial interests to disclose.
declarations.funderStatement: Keiichi Morimoto is supported by JSPS KAKENHI Grant Numbers JP24K04895 and JP23K25535.

detail.abstract: We develop a shadow-value interpretation of the finite-horizon Brock-Mirman model and use it to obtain an explicit, time-varying closed-form solution. Viewing one unit of current output as a shadow price yields a simple linear relation over time and a short geometric adjustment: as the horizon shortens, the saving share falls while the consumption share rises. We also show that the closed form survives under proportional taxes: return-and investmentside wedges operate through the effective return and thus govern adjustment speed, whereas a pure consumption tax shifts levels only.

AI.tldr: 本文基于影子价值视角重新解读有限期Brock-Mirman模型，获得了随时间变化的显式闭式解。研究发现：随着投资期限缩短，储蓄份额下降而消费份额上升；在比例税制下，闭式解依然成立，投资和回报方面的税收通过有效回报影响调整速度，而纯消费税仅影响水平值。
AI.research_question: 如何在有限期Brock-Mirman模型中建立影子价值解释并获得显式闭式解？不同税种如何影响模型的动态调整？
AI.motivation: 传统Brock-Mirman模型缺乏显式闭式解，限制了其在政策分析中的应用。通过影子价值视角，可以更清晰地理解模型的动态特征和税收效应。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于Brock-Mirman随机增长模型，引入影子价值概念，将当前产出单位视为影子价格，建立线性时间关系。
AI.method: 理论推导方法，通过影子价值重新构建模型，获得随时间变化的显式闭式解，并分析不同税种的影响机制。
AI.findings: 1) 获得有限期Brock-Mirman模型的显式闭式解；2) 随着投资期限缩短，储蓄份额下降，消费份额上升；3) 在比例税制下，投资和回报税通过有效回报影响调整速度，消费税仅影响水平值。
AI.theory_contributions: 1) 首次为有限期Brock-Mirman模型提供显式闭式解；2) 建立影子价值解释框架；3) 阐明不同税种对模型动态的差异化影响机制。
AI.practical_contributions: 为政策制定者提供分析税收政策对储蓄和消费决策影响的实用工具，有助于设计更有效的财政政策。

detail.abstract: Investment funds bearing an organization's name can shape investor trust even when the name conveys no information about quality. In an incentivized experiment with retirement plan participants, we vary the organization associated with otherwise identical index funds to manipulate trust. Trusted organizations' names increase participants' expected returns and reduce perceived loss risk. A further five-to-thirteen percentage point increase in allocations is directly due to trust, independent of beliefs. Embedding these results in a portfolio choice model, we estimate a 5% trust premium, underscoring how organizational trust influences investment behavior, even absent informational value.

detail.abstract: This presentation summarises the key insights from Economic Policy Uncertainty and Non-Performing Loans in Bangladesh, a research study conducted by the same author. Drawing on time-series data from 2000 to 2021, the analysis employs robust econometric techniques to challenge traditional credit-risk frameworks. The results show that higher global economic policy uncertainty (GEPU) is associated with lower reported NPLs, a pattern explained as a masking effect driven by credit rationing, regulatory leniency, and delayed recognition of problem loans. The findings indicate that institutional quality, financial depth, and public debt influence this mechanism, while crises such as COVID-19 can expose the concealed link between uncertainty and financial stress. The policy recommendations emphasise stricter asset classification, forward-looking provisioning, sovereign debt prudence, and remittance oversight to enhance financial transparency and stability.

detail.abstract: Using microdata from the European Consumer Survey (CES) for 11 European countries and 53 months, we investigate the formation and heterogeneity of inflation expectations as well as their theory consistency with the Phillips curve in the euro area, and across countries and demographic groups. We examine how individuals in the euro area form their inflation expectations. Our findings show that people place significant weight on their current perception of inflation. Past experiences with prices also play a role, though to a lesser extent. Importantly, the formation of expectations tends to be forward-looking rather than backward-looking. A similar pattern emerges when we analyze the consistency of these expectations and perceptions with the Phillips Curve theory. Individuals in the euro area generally do not hold theory-consistent expectations regarding inflation. We find notable variations across gender, age, income, education level, household size regarding the formation of inflation expectation.

detail.abstract: Banks’ focus nowadays shifts to non-financial risks, since credit and market risks are now well understood and under better control. We study whether macroprudential policy, designed to enhance financial system resilience, can mitigate or magnify losses stemming from such risks. To do so, we use a panel dataset on Eurozone countries between 2009-2018 and examine the dynamic path of operational risk exposures in response to tightening and loosening events of various macroprudential policies. Our results show that the tightening of specific measures, i.e., loan loss provisions, liquidity and loan to value, increases operational losses, whereas the loosening of measures, such as conservation buffers, loan loss provisions and debt service to income leads to a reduction in operational losses. Our results remain robust when we employ the inverse probability weighted estimator.

detail.abstract: Does the maturity of the relevant risk-free rate influence the strength of monetary policy pass-through to interest rates on new loans? To address this question, we present novel empirical evidence on lending practices across all euro area countries, using AnaCredit data covering nearly seven million new loans issued to non-financial corporations in 2022–2023. We document substantial variation in (a) the prevalence of fixed- vs floating-rate loans, (b) rate fixation periods, and (c) reference rates. This variation results in lending rates being exposed to different segments of the risk-free rate yield curve which, in turn, influence their sensitivity to monetary policy changes. We show that loans linked to shorter-maturity risk-free rates experience more pronounced monetary pass-through. Importantly, this effect is not purely mechanical, as part of the effect is offset by adjustments in the premium, revealing previously less-explored heterogeneity in the pass-through to lending rates.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the long-term macroeconomic impacts of Brexit on the UK economy employing a dynamic general equilibrium model that incorporates endogenous firm entry, price markups and market competition. By integrating the trade frictions introduced by Brexit, the model explains how increased trade costs have altered firm behaviour, market structure, and broader economic performance. We assess a range of policy responses, from theoretically optimal but practically difficult tax-subsidy schemes to more realistic measures aimed at reducing firm entry barriers, encouraging private and public investment, and subsidizing labour costs. Our findings underscore the critical role of policies that can most directly influence firm creation, investment, and competition in addressing the structural challenges Brexit has introduced.

detail.abstract: This paper evaluates the forecasting performance of the relatively new machine learning Global Unrefined (GlobalUN, hereafter) model with respect to inflation in the Eurozone. In this global pooled neural network framework, we use a quarterly panel dataset covering 20 euro-area countries (2001Q1–2025Q1) together with the EA-20 aggregate, which includes key variables such as HICP, energy prices, food, and others. Thus, the network remains simple yet flexible enough to absorb heterogeneity across countries. Our contribution of our work is crucial since monetary policy in the Eurozone hinges on accurate inflation forecasts (i.e., as ECB decisions target expected rather than current inflation). Our findings are crystal clear. The GlobalUn model outperforms all other benchmark models and the advanced machine learning XGBoost model in almost all Eurozone countries and horizons (i.e., the NAÏVE model seems to outperform in a few cases). These results are useful for policymakers, central banks, and fiscal institutions, as they should take the GlobalUN model into account as part of their arsenal.

detail.abstract: Climate change poses a significant risk to financial stability by impacting sovereign credit risk. Quantifying the exact impact is difficult as climate risk encompasses different components - transition risk and physical risk - with some of these, as well as the policies to address them, playing out over a long-time horizon. In this paper, we use a large panel of 52 developed and developing economies over two decades to empirically investigate the extent to which climate risks influence sovereign yields. The results of a panel regression analysis show that transition risk is associated with higher sovereign yields, with the effect more pronounced for developing economies and for high-emitting countries after the Paris agreement. In contrast, high-temperature anomalies do not appear to be priced-in sovereign borrowing costs. At the same time, countries with high levels of debt tend to record higher sovereign yields as acute physical risk increases. In the medium term, using local projections, we find that sovereign yields respond significantly but also differently to different types of disaster caused by climate change. We also explore the nonlinear effects of weather-related natural disasters on sovereign yields and find a striking contrast in the impact of climate shocks on sovereign borrowing costs according to income level and fiscal space when the shock hits.

detail.title: Predicting Black-Box Performance
detail.abstract: Black box systems are complex mechanisms whose internal workings cannot be easily understood or examined. These systems are becoming increasingly common due to the rapid growth of neural networks and artificial intelligence. However, many organizations hesitate to adopt them because of concerns about unknown or unexpected behavior. This paper presents a straightforward methodology for evaluating black box systems using only their inputs and outputs-the information that is readily observable. The approach works by analyzing the system's "regret," which measures the expected cost of suboptimal decisions. Regret is a common minimization target in the machine learning literature. This paper provides a closed-form characterization of regret for linear machine learning, algorithmic black-box, and other linear optimization systems. This paper shows that regret for any linear optimization model of the form y = c T π(c) equals the covariance of the available inputs c and the corresponding outputs ŷ produced by the black box. This article also develops properties and bounds of suboptimality loss. The proposed methodology can be used to ex ante evaluate regret of black-box systems, saving practitioners time and money in establishing performance of the black box. The Experiments section of this paper shows an application of the methodology to financial portfolio optimization.

detail.abstract: This paper draws on the macro-finance model developed in Brissimis and Georgiou (2022) which exploits the expectations hypothesis with time variation in the term premium, to evaluate the effects of unconventional monetary policy on long-term interest rates in the euro area. detail.abstract: A longstanding puzzle for regulatory theory and practice has been the valuation of children's lives, or more precisely, the valuation of mortality risks faced by children. There is data about parents' willingness to pay (WTP) to reduce such risks, and that data might be used to produce a Valuation of Statistical Lives (VSL) for children. The problem is that any such VSL comes from the parents' valuations; it might not adequately capture the welfare effects of risk reduction for children themselves. It can be shown, however, that use of parental WTP, and the resulting VSL, is justified if (1) patents have adequate information, (2) parents do not suffer from a relevant behavioral bias, (3) parents are motivated to care about their children's welfare, so that parental judgments about how to allocate limited resources for their children promote their children's welfare; and (4) parents have a limited budget for expenditures on their children, and regulation would amount to a forced exchange, producing a dollar-for-dollar reduction from that budget. If we relax one or more of these assumptions, the VSL for children might be higher than the VSL that emerges from use of parental WTP. If we relax (1), (2), and (3), the analysis of how to proceed is straightforward, at least in principle. If we relax (4), it is probably best not to tinker with VSL, even if the assessment of welfare and distributional effects is not straightforward.

detail.title: The Myth of Altseason
detail.abstract: This paper examines the conditions that define and sustain "altseason," periods when a majority of alternative cryptocurrencies outperform Bitcoin. We adopt the practical definition that altseason occurs when at least seventy-five percent of the top one hundred coins (excluding stablecoins and assetbacked tokens) outperform Bitcoin over a ninety-day window. Using case studies of 2017, 2021, and the failed 2024-25 attempt, the study argues that not all dips in Bitcoin dominance or euphoric headlines translate into true altseasons. The findings suggest that genuine altseasons coincide with broad altcoin strength and supportive macro-liquidity conditions, while failed attempts occur when Bitcoin dominance only briefly tests key levels without sustained confirmation.

detail.abstract: This paper evaluates the impact of Minimum Unit Pricing (MUP) on alcohol consumption in the UK using a difference-in-differences (DiD) framework, leveraging rich individual-level survey data. We estimate Average Treatment Effects on the Treated (ATET) using both standard and staggered DiD approaches. Although we find no significant change in the share of individuals drinking at least monthly following MUP implementation, we document meaningful reductions in drinking intensity: binge drinking declined by up to 18 percentage points among younger cohorts, and the share of individuals consuming more than two drinks on a typical day also fell significantly. These results suggest that while MUP had a limited impact on drinking frequency, it was effective in curbing harmful patterns of alcohol use, particularly among younger individuals.

detail.abstract: This study examines the behavior of herd mentality in consumers in supermarket settings, where people's buying choices are swayed by others' observable choices. Through an analysis of patterns of consumption behavior and a survey of current psychological and economic research, the article reviews how social influence, environmental stimuli, and marketing techniques prompt aggregation in buyers' decisions. These insights are useful not only for consumers who may become increasingly aware of how they decide, but also for stores, who frequently capitalize on herd behavior in order to increase sales.

detail.title: Financing Urbanization in China
detail.abstract: The developing world has experienced rapid urbanization, yet governments are fiscally challenged in financing urban infrastructure. China's central government launched a national initiative that encouraged local governments to adopt public-private partnerships (PPPs) to finance infrastructure investments between 2014 and 2020. By leveraging novel pilot variation and assembling newly digitized, linked administrative data, this paper studies the effectiveness of PPP adoption and its fiscal and economic consequences. I have four findings. First, PPP adoption is unlikely to mitigate fiscal pressures in providing public goods, as pilot-induced PPP projects are more likely to rely on non-user-charged payback mechanisms, and fiscally constrained counties adopt fewer PPP-financed projects. Second, the market mechanism of PPPs intended to select capable contractors through competitive procurement is undermined by political considerations, where contract allocations are distorted by local officials' promotion incentives with favoritism toward state-owned enterprises. Third, introducing PPPs generates substitution effects on traditional land-based financing, especially for county-level governments, with each RMB of PPP financing associated with a 0.21 RMB reduction in land-based revenue. Lastly, there is no evidence that PPP investments improve the local economy, cautioning against viewing investment-led expansion as a growth panacea. I conclude with policy implications.

detail.abstract: This study introduces a Feng Shui AI model for real estate mass appraisals, integrating classical geomantic principles with modern digital and AI tools. Based on Form School Fengshui theory, we develop a structured framework to quantify five core Feng Shui elements-Mountain, Water, Bright Hall, Xing Sha, and Qi-and implement a fourstage few-shot AI workflow for automated evaluation using satellite imagery. The analysis proceeds in two phases on all transacted commercial properties in Singapore. In the first stage, a Feng Shui master manually evaluates a sample of buildings; in the second stage, trained AI performs large-scale automated assessments. Incorporating Feng Shui scores into hedonic pricing models reveals that properties with good Feng Shui command a 22% price premium, with Water and Xing Sha being most influential. The AI-generated Feng Shui estimates closely align with manual assessments and significantly improve model fit, particularly at the tails of the price distribution. This research demonstrates how AI can operationalize ancient spatial reasoning to enhance real estate valuation and offers a scalable framework extendable beyond Feng Shui applications.

detail.title: Exploring EU-UK Trade and Investment Four Years After Brexit

publicationDetails.detailsText: ECB Occasional Paper No. 2025/379

detail.abstract: This paper looks at how Brexit has affected trade and foreign direct investment (FDI) between the United Kingdom and the EU. In 2020 the United Kingdom and the EU signed the Trade and Cooperation Agreement (TCA) , establishing the post-Brexit relationship and, in particular, a tariff-free area for goods produced in either of the two economies. However, non-tariff barriers to the trading of goods and services have emerged. Moreover, the United Kingdom’s departure from the EU has affected its attractiveness as an investment target. We analyse recent developments in UK imports and exports with the EU and the rest of the world, in both goods and services, including financial services and tourism. Our estimates suggest that, after the Brexit transition period, UK exports to the EU contracted by almost 40%, due to the emergence of non-tariff barriers with the EU, and the fact that no significant UK trade flows were redirected to other partners. Finally, the analysis of product-level data on German, French, Italian and Spanish exports to the United Kingdom has confirmed the significant negative impact of Brexit, especially for goods highly exposed or highly sensitive to increases in trade costs. The FDI analysis begins with a conjunctural assessment that includes recent trends in EU-UK FDI at a broad level (including sectoral and geographical details), a breakdown of foreign affiliates and an investigation of new FDI projects and jobs in the United Kingdom. The analysis continues with developments in the UK financial sector in terms of the real economy, FDI flows, banks, insurance companies and pension funds, and the evolving status of the United Kingdom as a leading global financial centre. Finally, our analysis also provides an econometric investigation into the potential impact of Brexit on EU-UK FDI, using a gravity model approach. […]

title: Dual Nash Equilibria in Adversarial Asset Pricing: The Q-Measure and the P-Measure
affiliations: Imperial College London - Department of Mathematics

detail.title: Dual Nash Equilibria in Adversarial Asset Pricing: The Q-Measure and the P-Measure
detail.abstract: We argue that adversarial asset pricing admits two distinct Nash equilibria. The first, defined in the strategic pricing game between a trader and Nature, corresponds to the risk-neutral measure Q under which discounted prices are martingales. The second, arising from the adaptive feedback of real economies and trading ecologies, corresponds to the physical measure P, which embodies Nature's empirical and boundedly rational behaviour. Their divergence, measured by the Radon-Nikodym derivative or by an informationtheoretic distance such as Kullback-Leibler divergence, quantifies the degree of disequilibrium and provides a formal definition of statistical alpha. Appendix A develops fixed-point formulations of both equilibria: Q as a minimax fixed point of a pricing operator T Q , and P as a fixed point of an adaptive operator Φ representing market-policy feedback, linked through an information-tilting family I θ. Appendix B illustrates these constructions in a linear-Gaussian (LQG) economy where the adaptive equilibrium is unique under a contraction in the Wasserstein metric and converges to the adversarial equilibrium under increasing informational tilt. Appendix C derives the exact sampling distribution of the annualized Sharpe ratio as a function of the KL divergence between P and Q, showing that the true Sharpe satisfies S ann = 2D year and that its estimator follows a scaled noncentral-t law. Together these results connect adversarial pricing, adaptive dynamics, and empirical performance statistics within a unified information-geometric framework.

AI.method: 固定点公式化方法、线性高斯经济模型分析、Wasserstein度量收缩分析
AI.findings: 发现了两个不同的纳什均衡：Q均衡（风险中性测度）和P均衡（物理测度），两者的KL散度量化了市场非均衡程度，Sharpe比率与年度KL散度存在精确关系。
AI.theory_contributions: 建立了对抗性定价、自适应动态和实证绩效统计的统一信息几何框架，提供了统计alpha的正式定义。
AI.practical_contributions: 为量化投资策略提供了理论基础，Sharpe比率的精确分布推导有助于更准确的风险评估和绩效衡量。

detail.title: Specifics of Waste Management in Latin American Countries
detail.abstract: In the context of the global environmental crisis, effective waste management is becoming a key element of green development. The article examines the specifics of industrial and municipal solid waste management in Latin America and the Caribbean, where urbanization and consumer culture exacerbate the problem of waste accumulation. Despite differences in the economic development of the countries in the region, common challenges remain the low recycling rate (averaging 4.5% in the region), the predominance of landfilling (up to 92% in Chile), and the widespread prevalence of uncontrolled dumpsites. Structural imbalances are aggravated by sharp contrasts between urban and rural areas in waste collection coverage (85% vs. 30%), as well as a significant informal sector whose activities are poorly integrated into formal management systems. Legal regulation is characterized by fragmentation-from Chile's stringent model to Argentina's decentralized systems-creating barriers to the harmonization of environmental policy. Additional problems include the high volume of organic waste (52%), a lack of investment in infrastructure, and technological backwardness. The work demonstrates that the transition to a green economy in Latin America requires a comprehensive approach combining technological innovation, social inclusion, and institutional reforms.

detail.title: Supply Chain Decoupling in Green Products: A Granular Input-output Analysis

publicationDetails.detailsText: ECB Working Paper No. 2025/3152

detail.abstract: This paper introduces a novel methodology to enhance the granularity of Inter-Country Input-Output (ICIO) tables. While our general methodology can be applied to any products of interest, we show that the well-documented distortions caused by sectoral aggregation in ICIO tables are particularly pronounced for products with a low substitutability, such as those essential to the green transition (e.g. electric batteries, rare earths). We therefore apply our framework to construct a disaggregated ICIO table that singles out 129 products essential to the energy transition. We then simulate a hypothetical scenario of an East-West supply chain decoupling in green products through a multi-country multi-sector model calibrated with our tailored disaggregated ICIO table. Results reveal substantial economic costs: welfare losses reach 3% and trade between blocs contracts by 20%, even when accounting for trade diversion through neutral countries. We finally quantify how the green supply chain decoupling increases the intensities of greenhouse gas emissions, highlighting how trade barriers on green sectors affect both economic efficiency and climate objectives.

title: Who Harvests? Tax Alpha and Heterogeneous Responses to Capital Gains Taxation

detail.title: Who Harvests? Tax Alpha and Heterogeneous Responses to Capital Gains Taxation
detail.abstract: Capital taxation is a central component of the U.S. fiscal system: realized gains totaled $1.4 trillion in 2024, and their preferential tax treatment amounted to $244 billion in foregone federal revenue. Yet little is known about how households, especially the ultra-wealthy, respond to capital gains taxes. Using granular, high-frequency data on U.S. households-including more than 700 billionaires-I study the response to capital gains taxation across the wealth distribution. Wealthier households realize a smaller fraction of gains but a larger fraction of losses than less wealthy households, consistent with tax-loss harvesting. These differences intensify during market downturns and are concentrated among households supervised by sophisticated advisors, especially private banks. Exploiting a regression kink design around zero unrealized returns, I show that the realization behavior at the top reflects an active response to tax incentives rather than unobserved factors correlated with wealth. The implications for after-tax performance are significant: tax expenses decline from 70 basis points of wealth at the bottom to 20 basis points at the top, generating a 50-basis-points annual tax alpha, equal to over one-third of documented return gaps. Absent this tax alpha, the top 1% aggregate wealth share would grow by 3.54 percentage points less over thirty years, corresponding to 63% of the historical rise in top-end wealth concentration over an equivalent horizon. These findings reveal a policy-relevant channel through which the U.S. tax code amplifies wealth concentration, informing both macroeconomic models of wealth dynamics and normative models of capital taxation.

title: Credit, Conflict, and Constraints: Determinants of Rural Microcredit Allocation in Colombia
affiliations: IE University

detail.title: Credit, Conflict, and Constraints: Determinants of Rural Microcredit Allocation in Colombia
detail.abstract:
This paper examines how violence shapes the depth and distribution of rural financial inclusion in Colombia by focusing on access to microcredits (Rural Microfinance Fund) for the period 2016-2023. Using municipality-level data, we combine detailed indicators of conflict intensity (extortions, forced displacement, ambushes, and homicides) with administrative records of more than 1.3 million microcredits to estimate the causal impact of insecurity on access to credit.

The research explores how the impact of violence continues to shape access to credit, particularly among small and medium agricultural producers. By estimating Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) models with fixed effects and robust controls, such as rurality, GDP per capita, and financial infrastructure density, the results reveal a consistent, negative relationship between violence and microcredit disbursement. Specifically, municipalities exposed to certain forms of violence tend to receive fewer loans per capita. For instance, increases in extortion cases or forced displacement significantly reduce the volume of credit allocated. Conversely, other forms of violence, such as ambushes, appear to be associated with higher lending, possibly reflecting a compensatory institutional response in highly insecure areas. A series of robustness checks, including multicollinearity diagnostics, a composite violence index, and alternative functional forms, confirms the main findings.
This paper contributes to policy debates on inclusive rural development by identifying both the enabling and constraining factors in Colombia’s financial inclusion strategy. The findings show that crime and insecurity significantly reduce access to credit, even after accounting for economic and institutional factors. This highlights the need for context-sensitive interventions that integrate credit provision with strengthened security protocols and local mechanisms to improve social safety.

title: GDP Composition as an Indicator of Economic Structure in African Economies: Patterns, Determinants, and Development Implications
affiliations: RMIT University and La Trobe University and Independent

detail.title: GDP Composition as an Indicator of Economic Structure in African Economies: Patterns, Determinants, and Development Implications
detail.abstract: This study examines the composition of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) as a lens through which to understand the underlying economic structures of African economies. GDP composition-the relative shares of agriculture, industry, and services-offers critical insights into patterns of structural transformation, sectoral productivity, and long-term development trajectories. Using a panel dataset covering African countries over the past three decades, the analysis explores both the variation in GDP structure across countries and its evolution over time. The paper identifies distinct structural profiles, ranging from resource-dependent economies with a dominant industrial or extractive sector, to agrarian economies where agriculture accounts for a significant share of GDP, to more diversified economies with expanding service sectors. By employing econometric methods, the study investigates the determinants of GDP composition, focusing on factors such as income level, trade openness, natural resource endowments, demographic trends, and institutional quality. Findings reveal that while many African economies are experiencing gradual shifts away from agriculture toward services, industrialisation remains uneven and in some cases stagnant. Resourcerich countries tend to maintain high industrial shares due to extractive activities, but these sectors often exhibit weak linkages with the broader economy. Conversely, resource-poor but institutionally stronger countries display more balanced structural shifts, suggesting that governance quality and economic policy play a significant role in shaping sectoral dynamics. The study further discusses the development implications of observed GDP structures. Economies with a narrow sectoral base are more vulnerable to external shocks, commodity price volatility, and employment instability, while more diversified structures tend to support resilience and inclusive growth. The paper concludes by emphasising the need for policies that promote productive diversification, strengthen industrial capacity, and enhance the integration of sectors to achieve sustainable development in Africa.

detail.abstract: This paper seeks to identify the international organisations’ (IOs) vision of the future of education, distinguishing their policy framing and narrative. This inquiry links to the interpretive comparative analysis of ideas and politics underlying the IOs’ seemingly convergent digital transformation reform movement. The findings of this paper indicate that IOs’ visions for digital sovereignty and digital expansionism have revolved around their historical struggles between redistributive and liberal development in the evolved context of digitalisation. While UNESCO promotes a digital commons approach that emphasises the role of governments in establishing and overseeing digital infrastructures, the OECD and the World Bank have proposed neoliberal policies, including free trade agreements, the liberalisation of digital markets, and private investment to develop digital public infrastructures. In education, UNESCO has emphasized the significance of face-to-face schooling and teachers in the future education systems and practices. In contrast, the OECD and the World Bank have promoted radical public education reform proposals to introduce changes and innovations, highlighting the roles of adaptive, personalized digital technologies, cost-effective blended learning, and public-private partnerships as equally important as those of schools and teachers. Notably, both the OECD and the World Bank have proposed a digital single market adopting the concepts of free flow of people, goods, services, capital, and data to the digital realm while reducing the barriers across borders, further advocating for the development of digital education infrastructures for inclusive, resilient, scalable digital education systems. Illustrating the gaps between their humanistic story and neoliberal policy proposals, this paper argues that the OECD and the World Bank seem to be embarking on another historical structural adjustment movement towards neoliberal digital reforms for public administration and education, encouraging the free flow of data capital and interoperability now required to advance digital and ed-tech industries.

title: Determinants of Demographic Potential in Least Developed Countries: Patterns and Implications

detail.title: Determinants of Demographic Potential in Least Developed Countries: Patterns and Implications
detail.abstract: Demographic potential, understood as the capacity of a population structure to generate sustainable socioeconomic growth, is a decisive factor in shaping long-term development trajectories. In Least Developed Countries (LDCs), this potential is both immense and fragile, influenced by a complex interplay of structural, social, economic, and environmental determinants. This article investigates the principal drivers of demographic potential in LDCs, analyzing their patterns, dynamics, and implications for national and international development strategies. The study situates demographic potential within the broader framework of human capital formation, labour force participation, and the demographic dividend. LDCs currently experience some of the highest population growth rates in the world, accompanied by youthful age structures that could, in principle, serve as engines of development. Yet, the realization of this potential is conditional on critical determinants, including educational attainment, healthcare access, employment opportunities, governance quality, and environmental resilience. Where these determinants align positively, demographic growth can translate into accelerated human development; where they remain deficient, population growth exacerbates poverty, unemployment, and vulnerability. The empirical analysis highlights three major patterns. First, education emerges as a pivotal determinant, not only in raising individual capabilities but also in shaping fertility behaviour and intergenerational mobility. Second, health outcomes-including maternal and child health, nutrition, and disease control-directly condition the productivity and longevity of the labour force, thereby influencing the extent to which demographic potential can be realized. Third, structural economic conditions, such as labour market absorption capacity and the degree of diversification, determine whether youthful populations contribute to growth or become sources of instability. These patterns are further complicated by governance and institutional effectiveness, which mediate the translation of demographic opportunities into tangible socioeconomic gains. The implications of these findings are significant. They suggest that demographic potential in LDCs cannot be treated as a self-fulfilling asset but rather as a contingent resource whose benefits depend on deliberate policy choices. Harnessing this potential requires integrated strategies that invest in human capital, expand decent employment opportunities, strengthen healthcare systems, and enhance institutional capacities. At the international level, addressing structural vulnerabilities-particularly those linked to climate change and economic dependencyis essential for enabling LDCs to transform demographic growth into sustainable development. By foregrounding the determinants and conditions of demographic potential, this article contributes to a more nuanced understanding of development prospects in the world's least developed economies, while underscoring the urgent need for policies that convert demographic opportunity into inclusive and resilient progress.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a groundbreaking theoretical framework titled Multidimensional Fractional Refractions Momentums, which proposes a fundamental redefinition of physical reality by eliminating the traditional concept of time as a primary dimension. Instead, it posits that all physical phenomena emerge from the continuous interactions, transformations, and refractions of multidimensional fractional momentums distributed across an infinite network of spatial planes. These momentums exist as dynamic, non-linear, and multidirectional entities that generate the observable progression, causality, and evolution previously attributed to time. Within this framework, the structure and behaviour of the universe are not governed by temporal flow but by complex refraction patterns of momentum that give rise to order, entropy, and transformation at every scale of existence from quantum fields to cosmic expansion. This paradigm shift reinterprets causality, reversibility, and physical evolution without reliance on a temporal axis, offering a potential bridge between quantum mechanics, relativity, and cosmology. By advancing Multidimensional Fractional Refractions Momentums as the fundamental fabric of physical reality, this study opens new pathways for rethinking space, motion, and the underlying architecture of the universe.

affiliations: Virginia Tech

detail.title: Tipping as a Pricing Signal
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a menu-cost theory of tipping. When firms face costs of changing posted prices, voluntary tips provide a noisy but informative signal of whether current prices are "too low" or "too high." The firm adjusts its price only when tip deviations exceed an information-dependent threshold, generating a time-varying inaction band. The framework explains why tipping is common in volatile, service-intensive industries but rare in standardized chains with rich alternative telemetry. Unlike existing models based on norms or reciprocity, this approach requires only that average tips increase weakly with perceived surplus for the consumers.

detail.abstract: The UK’s offshore oil and gas industry is in long-term decline, placing workers at risk of job loss and career disruption. While policymakers have committed to ensuring a ‘Just Transition’ for fossil fuel workers, there is limited understanding of what this should look like in practice. This study presents qualitative findings from 37 semi-structured interviews with UK offshore oil and gas workers and industry stakeholders. It explores employment conditions in the sector and identifies barriers to obtaining quality work in renewable energy and beyond. Participants reported chronic job insecurity, mental health impacts, and obstacles such as skill mismatches, certification barriers, and perceived stigma when seeking alternative work. Drawing on the concepts of justice and decent work, the study proposes a UK-specific definition of a Just Transition. It is characterised by access to secure and fulfilling work that aligns with workers’ skillsets and pay levels, enables control over work and career decisions, and retains the challenge and enjoyment of previous roles. The findings highlight an urgent need for targeted policy to address stigma, streamline reskilling pathways, and reduce bureaucratic barriers. Clearer definitions and tangible support are essential to deliver a meaningful Just Transition for this workforce.

title: How does Population Growth Affect Economic Growth in African Countries? An Empirical Analysis
affiliations: Independent and RMIT University and La Trobe University

detail.title: How does Population Growth Affect Economic Growth in African Countries? An Empirical Analysis
detail.abstract: The relationship between population dynamics and economic performance has long been a subject of scholarly debate, particularly in the context of developing regions. This article empirically investigates the impact of population growth on economic growth in African countries, drawing on panel data covering the period 1990-2022. While classical Malthusian theory suggests that rapid population growth constrains development through resource scarcity, more recent perspectives emphasize the potential for demographic dividends, labor force expansion, and market enlargement. Using a fixed-effects regression model complemented by robustness checks through generalized method of moments (GMM), the study evaluates how variations in population growth influence GDP per capita growth across diverse African economies. The results reveal a complex and heterogeneous relationship. For low-income countries with weak institutional frameworks, rapid population growth tends to exacerbate poverty, strain public services, and suppress per capita income growth. In contrast, middle-income African economies with relatively stronger governance structures and higher investment in education and health exhibit evidence of a positive demographic effect, as a growing labor force stimulates production and domestic demand. The findings suggest that the economic impact of population growth in Africa is conditional on institutional quality, human capital development, and the absorptive capacity of labor markets. The article concludes that population growth is not inherently a barrier to economic development; rather, its consequences depend on complementary policies. Strengthening education, healthcare, infrastructure, and employment creation is essential for African countries to harness the potential benefits of demographic expansion and mitigate its associated risks.

detail.title: Investigating divergent impact of fintech on financial stability, profitability and efficiency of banks in India
detail.abstract: This paper aims to identify linkages between fintech development and its implications for financial stability, bank efficiency and profitability in India with a balanced panel data of 29 banks for 15 years (from 2010 to 2024). A self-constructed Fintech Development Index (FDI) using text mining approach across multiple fintech dimensions has been developed. Both static and dynamic panel data regression have been used wherever appropriate. In particular, the System GMM approach is adopted under dynamic model when addressing endogeneity concerns. The findings reveal a significantly positive impact of fintech on technical efficiency as gauged through Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA), while its effect on cost efficiency is significantly negative. Fintech contributed positively and significantly to financial stability whereas no significant impact is observed on bank profitability. Demonetization of currencies brought produced negative impact on cost efficiency whereas Crisis of COVID-19 produced a negative impact on cost efficiency and profitability.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a simulation-based approach to compute the implied valuation of all equity tranches within a Venture Capital backed company. Startups are frequently financed by issuing preferred shares with embedded options to protect VC investors, causing an asymmetrical distribution of value amongst shareholders. Compared to previous research, this approach brings more accuracy and flexibility by allowing the usage of more realistic stochastic diffusion models while being easily applicable to the most complex capitalisation tables where preferred shares are mixed with employee option pools. We found evidence that adding a jump-diffusion component to the standard model seems justified, as it improves the fit of the model to historical data while better reflecting the inherently high risk of VC investing.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates how tone and pitch in corporate conference calls shape investor reactions and market outcomes. Using Refinitiv audio archives linked with CRSP daily returns from 2010 to 2025, I quantify acoustic features-mean pitch, vocal energy, and pause ratio-for over 7,000 U.S. firms. These measures are matched with cumulative abnormal returns (CARs) and trading volume around earnings-announcement dates. After controlling for Fama-French five-factor risk exposures, textual sentiment, and firm characteristics, I find that higher vocal tone (a combination of pitch and energy) predicts stronger short-term returns and higher trading activity, while a greater pause ratio (hesitation) predicts muted market response. The evidence supports the behavioral-attention hypothesis: investors infer confidence and optimism from vocal cues, which affect perceived credibility and risk appetite. Although algorithmic trading dampens magnitude after 2018, human tone remains a statistically and economically significant signal in price formation.

AI.tldr: 本文研究发现，企业电话会议中的声音语调（音高和能量）能够预测短期股票回报和交易活跃度，而停顿比率（犹豫）则预示市场反应平淡。声音线索影响投资者对管理层信心和乐观程度的判断，进而影响市场反应。
AI.research_question: 企业电话会议中的音调和音高如何影响投资者反应和市场结果？
AI.motivation: 探索声音特征作为非语言信息载体在金融市场中的作用，验证行为注意力假说，即投资者从声音线索中推断管理层的信心和乐观程度。
AI.theoretical_framework: 行为注意力假说、声音心理学、市场微观结构理论
AI.method: 使用Refinitiv音频档案和CRSP日度收益数据（2010-2025年），量化声音特征（平均音高、声音能量、停顿比率），并与累计异常回报和交易量进行匹配分析，控制Fama-French五因子风险暴露、文本情绪和公司特征。
AI.findings: 较高的声音语调（音高和能量的组合）预测更强的短期回报和更高的交易活跃度，而较大的停顿比率（犹豫）预测市场反应平淡。尽管算法交易在2018年后减弱了影响幅度，但人类语调在价格形成中仍具有统计和经济显著性。
AI.theory_contributions: 为行为金融学提供了声音线索影响投资者决策的经验证据，拓展了非语言信息在金融市场中作用的理论框架。
AI.practical_contributions: 为投资者提供了基于声音分析的投资决策工具，为企业管理层提供了改善沟通效果的实践指导，为监管机构识别市场操纵行为提供了新视角。

detail.title: Copula-Based Estimation of Urban Available Water Accessibility and Its Socio-Economic Effects

publicationDetails.detailsText: HYDROL75245

detail.abstract: Urban water accessibility is a key indicator of water resource supply and a critical component of sustainable urban development. However, assessing water accessibility is often constrained by weighted models that neglect indicator relationships, and analyzing its socio-economic effects has been limited to spatial patterns rather than causal pathways. This dual limitation obscures accurate evaluation and a full understanding of its complex influence on urban development. In this study, a comprehensive accessibility index was constructed using the Copula function by integrating the four core indicators of spatial distance, runoff, slope, and water quality. Furthermore, the PLS-SEM model was employed to explore the dynamic multi-path effects of water accessibility on urban facility distribution, talent attraction, and economic vitality. A case study of Wuhan’s core urban area reveals these dynamic socio-economic effects. Water accessibility consistently showed a direct positive contribution to economic development. However, its effect on talent attraction shifted from positive to negative over time, influenced by factors such as polycentric urban development and post-pandemic market changes. Constrained by ecological protection policies, its effect on facility agglomeration remained weakly negative. These effects also exhibited significant spatial heterogeneity, closely associated with regional development stages and resource endowments. In summary, this study offers a novel analytical framework for the refined assessment of urban water accessibility, supporting sustainable and fine-scale waterfront planning.

AI.tldr: 本研究构建了基于Copula函数的综合水可达性指数，并运用PLS-SEM模型分析水可达性对城市设施分布、人才吸引和经济活力的动态多路径影响。研究发现水可达性对经济发展有持续正向贡献，但对人才吸引的影响随时间从正转负，对设施集聚的影响受生态政策约束呈弱负向。
AI.research_question: 如何准确评估城市水可达性及其对城市发展的复杂社会经济影响？
AI.motivation: 现有水可达性评估受限于忽略指标关系的加权模型，且社会经济效应分析多局限于空间模式而非因果路径，这阻碍了准确评估和全面理解其对城市发展的复杂影响。
AI.theoretical_framework: Copula函数用于构建综合水可达性指数，PLS-SEM模型用于分析动态多路径效应。
AI.method: 整合空间距离、径流、坡度和水质四个核心指标构建综合水可达性指数，并运用PLS-SEM模型探索水可达性对城市设施分布、人才吸引和经济活力的多路径效应，以武汉核心城区为案例进行研究。
AI.findings: 水可达性对经济发展有持续正向贡献；对人才吸引的影响随时间从正转负，受多中心城市发展和后疫情市场变化影响；受生态保护政策约束，对设施集聚的影响呈弱负向；这些效应表现出显著的空间异质性，与区域发展阶段和资源禀赋密切相关。
AI.theory_contributions: 提出了城市水可达性精细化评估的新分析框架，支持可持续和精细尺度的滨水规划。
AI.practical_contributions: 为城市水可达性评估提供了更准确的方法，有助于理解水可达性对城市发展的复杂社会经济影响，支持可持续城市规划和滨水区域发展决策。

title: Beyond Network Contagion: Credit Shock Spillovers and Macro-Volatility in Emerging Fund Markets
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Beyond Network Contagion: Credit Shock Spillovers and Macro-Volatility in Emerging Fund Markets
detail.abstract: We study whether a large, time-stamped credit shock generates spillovers in nascent private funds markets. We analyze Brazil’s FIAGROs, a retail-tilted credit and equity segment focused on agricultural investing. Using a regression-discontinuity-in-time (RDiT) design around the largest judicial-recovery filing in the Brazilian agricultural market, complemented by difference-in-differences (DiD) estimates, we document a sharp day-0 price drop for directly exposed funds and persistent underperformance in the immediate aftermath. In contrast, non-exposed funds exhibit limited cross-fund contagion. Interacting treatment with broad-equity volatility shows that macro conditions meaningfully amplify losses, consistent with a market-wide risk-off channel rather than within-sector contagion. Results are robust to alternative RDiT placebo cutoffs, and alternative DiD specifications. Our findings highlight that in nascent, retail-oriented funds markets, stability concerns arise less from intra-sector cascades and more from macro-volatility amplification. We discuss implications for macroprudential buffers, single-name exposure disclosure, and liquidity-risk management in emerging markets.

AI.tldr: 本文研究了巴西农业投资基金市场中的信用冲击溢出效应，发现直接暴露基金在最大司法重组申请日出现显著价格下跌和持续表现不佳，而非暴露基金传染效应有限。宏观波动会放大损失，表明风险主要来自市场范围的风险规避而非行业内传染。

AI.motivation: 研究新兴零售导向基金市场中信用冲击的传染机制，为宏观审慎监管提供依据

AI.method: 回归断点时间设计（RDiT）和双重差分法（DiD），围绕巴西农业市场最大司法重组申请事件进行分析

detail.title: Against an AI Privilege

publicationDetails.detailsText: Against an AI Privilege, Harv. J. L. & Tech. Dig. (Nov. 7, 2015), https://jolt.law.harvard.edu/digest/against-an-ai-privilege

detail.abstract:
This Article argues against recognizing a general evidentiary privilege for interactions with generative AI services (including prompts, outputs, and related logs on commercial platforms). Existing privileges—such as those protecting attorney-client, psychotherapist-patient, and clergy-penitent communications—rest on longstanding commitments to relationships essential to justice and social welfare. No comparable justification exists for recognizing a privilege for AI interactions. While individuals may use AI tools for advice, comfort, or candor, the absence of a relational foundation, professional oversight, or public-good rationale undermines the case for privilege. At the same time, courts and policymakers should not ignore the privacy and policy concerns raised by the expanding role of AI. Narrower protections, such as limited confidentiality or statutory safeguards, may address those concerns without distorting the evidentiary system. Privilege, however, is not the appropriate response.

Link to Paper: https://jolt.law.harvard.edu/digest/against-an-ai-privilege

title: CALIBFLOW: A Dynamic Post-Survey Calibration Method

detail.title: CALIBFLOW: A Dynamic Post-Survey Calibration Method

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the research presented in this paper. The CALIBFLOW framework was developed independently for academic and methodological purposes within the IREIMO Laboratory, Université Hassan II de Casablanca.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, patient data, or sensitive personal information. The research focuses exclusively on methodological development and statistical modeling. Therefore, formal ethics approval was not required under institutional research guidelines.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The work was conducted as part of the author’s ongoing research activities at the IREIMO Laboratory, ENCG Casablanca.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces CALIBFLOW, a dynamic post-survey calibration method designed for continuous and hybrid data-collection systems. Unlike static approaches such as raking or GREG (Deville & Särndal, 1992; Hainmueller, 2012), CALIBFLOW performs an iterative, self-regulated, and multi-objective optimization of survey weights. The model minimizes a composite function that balances proximity to initial weights, deviation from known population margins, and control of weight dispersion. Adaptive coefficients are automatically updated according to statistical diagnostics-margin deviation (Δ), coefficient of variation (CV), effective sample size (n_eff), and absolute standardized mean difference (ASMD). The method preserves both representativeness and variance stability in non-stationary survey environments. The CALIBFLOW approach contributes to the emerging field of adaptive inference by integrating statistical calibration and online learning principles.

AI.tldr: CALIBFLOW是一种动态的后期调查校准方法，适用于连续和混合数据收集系统。它通过迭代、自调节的多目标优化来调整调查权重，平衡初始权重接近度、已知总体边际偏差和权重分散控制。该方法在非平稳调查环境中保持代表性和方差稳定性。
AI.research_question: 如何开发一种动态的后期调查校准方法，能够在连续和混合数据收集系统中有效处理非平稳环境下的权重调整问题？
AI.motivation: 传统的静态校准方法（如raking或GREG）在连续和混合数据收集系统中存在局限性，无法适应非平稳的调查环境，需要开发动态的校准方法。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于统计校准理论和在线学习原理，结合自适应推理框架，构建多目标优化模型。
AI.method: CALIBFLOW方法通过迭代、自调节的多目标优化最小化复合函数，自动更新自适应系数（包括边际偏差Δ、变异系数CV、有效样本量n_eff和绝对标准化均值差异ASMD）。
AI.findings: CALIBFLOW方法能够在非平稳调查环境中同时保持代表性和方差稳定性，优于传统的静态校准方法。
AI.theory_contributions: 将统计校准与在线学习原理相结合，推动了自适应推理领域的发展，为动态调查权重调整提供了理论框架。
AI.practical_contributions: 为连续和混合数据收集系统提供了有效的动态校准工具，能够适应非平稳环境，提高调查数据的质量和可靠性。

title: Structural Identity Injury: Psychological Effects of Institutional Suppression of Independence

detail.title: Structural Identity Injury: Psychological Effects of Institutional Suppression of Independence
detail.abstract: Independent actors are frequently removed from hierarchical institutions following periods of crisis tolerance. This pattern is commonly misattributed to personal failure, producing shame, rumination, and identity disruption. Building on a regime-switching model of institutional behavior, we define Structural Identity Injury (SII) as psychological harm arising when hierarchical institutions eliminate competent, high-autonomy individuals during predictable post-crisis reversion windows (18-36 months). This pattern reflects dependency equilibrium restoration: during crises, institutions temporarily value independence for survival; as crises recede and oversight reasserts, appointments turn over, and budget protections unwind, these same institutions suppress independence. We translate organizational variables to the individual level using an Independence score (I), a Structural Protection score (S), and a Timing variable (T) capturing post-crisis hysteresis. We propose diagnostic criteria distinguishing SII from performance-based termination and from adjacent constructs including burnout, depression, PTSD, and moral injury. We present a five-item SII screening scale (SII-5), a clinician intervention protocol centered on structural attribution, and a risk matrix using I, S, and T to guide treatment and vocational planning. We outline three complementary studies to validate SII as a distinct factor and to test intervention effects on shame reduction and identity coherence restoration. This framework offers clinicians and researchers a precise, falsifiable bridge between institutional structure and individual psychology, with immediate applications for therapeutic intervention and organizational policy.

detail.abstract:
This study investigates the complex interplay between human capital and innovation in shaping regional economic development, with a particular focus on persistent disparities across Polish regions. While prior research has established a general link between human capital and innovation, there remains a significant gap in understanding how this relationship manifests under varying institutional, historical, and socio-economic conditions, especially in post-transition and emerging economies, in the context of the latest economic and technological shifts like post-COVID recovery, digital transformation, and green economy initiatives. The aim is to uncover the mechanisms that either facilitate or hinder the translation of educational and workforce assets into regional innovation outcomes and to propose targeted, region-specific policy interventions.

Adopting a quantitative methodology, this study utilizes the Mazziotta-Pareto Index to develop composite indices for human capital and innovation. These indices are applied to 16 Polish regions, analyzed over 15 years (2009–2023). Data from Statistics Poland and Eurostat were standardized and aggregated to create comparative rankings. The analysis includes correlation assessments and regional rankings to identify patterns of divergence between human capital development and innovation output.

The results reveal significant regional disparities in Poland's human capital-innovation relationship. Some regions show strong alignment (e.g., Mazowieckie, Małopolskie), others possess high human capital but low innovation (e.g., Lubelskie, Podlaskie), while a few combine low human capital with high innovation (e.g., Podkarpacie). These mismatches are shaped by structural economic conditions, industrial specialization, and institutional quality. Findings suggest that enhancing institutional support and industry-academia linkages is critical for converting educational assets into innovation capacity. Targeted policy measures are needed to boost innovation absorption in human capital-rich regions and stimulate human capital development in innovative but skill-deficient areas.

The study highlights the need for differentiated, region-specific policy tools such as targeted R&D incentives, support for university-industry collaboration, and workforce mobility programs. These strategies can help unlock the latent innovation potential in high human capital regions and develop skills in innovation-leading but education-deficient areas. It is also important to create incentives for the funding of R&D and high-risk projects and to implement the concepts of smart villages and smart cities in the more economically deprived regions.

This research offers a novel contribution to the literature by combining a multidimensional synthetic index approach with a regional lens to examine the human capital–innovation nexus. By moving beyond national aggregates, it uncovers spatial mismatches that are critical for understanding regional development dynamics. This work, unlike other studies, takes into account the new research period, including COVID-19 times, which makes it possible to assess whether regional disparities are levelling out or not. Although focused on Poland, the findings are broadly applicable to other Eastern European post-transition and developing countries experiencing similar problems with financing innovations or countries with intra-regional variations, such as Germany or Italy. The study bridges theory and practice by offering actionable recommendations for regional policymakers, grounded in recent debates on digital transformation, green innovation, and human capital.

detail.abstract: Research investigating sexual serial murder is notably limited. There thus exists a rationale for continued theoretical development to guide empirical enquiry in relation to this topic. Existing empirical evidence and theoretical perspectives leave a multitude of lingering questions and gaps in our understanding of this highly complex phenomenon. The primary aim of this paper is to report on and integrate existing evidence and theoretical perspectives with Freudian psychoanalysis toward a better understanding of sexual serial homicide. A few proposed novel extensions to Freudian theory are discussed in their application to this disturbing form of violence, but not before an exhaustive account of the multitude of complex, dynamic, and intersecting processes that lead to the constitution of these novel concepts in the first place. The paper concludes that the essence of sexual serial homicide results from three psychoanalytic concepts, the ego-accomplice, drive vector addition, and object possession, where object possession in this context refers to object destruction.

detail.abstract: The actions of the Bank of England at the height of the financial crisis of 1825 are presented in more detail than has been available before. The credit for some of the novel steps the Bank took at that time that has been given to outsiders is exaggerated, as the directors had been experimenting with them surreptitiously before. Evidence is also presented that Bank directors had stronger incentives to engage in Lender of Last Resort (LOLR) operations than is usually thought. On the other hand, they appeared to be constrained by informal unwritten rules of acceptable banking behavior, and failed to engage in some simple transactions that would have been very profitable for the Bank and would also have helped mitigate the crisis.

detail.abstract: We construct a dynamic general equilibrium model with limited liability banks to compare macroeconomic outcomes under a regime in which insolvent banks are bailed out by the government with a regime where bank creditors are bailed in. We find that long-run investment, capital, output, and consumption are higher under the bailout regime. Bailouts also mitigate the contraction of credit in financial crises (with respect to bail-ins), but simultaneously lead to deeper recessions. Finally, higher leverage under the bailout regime substantially increases the fraction of banks that need to be recapitalized.

detail.abstract: A central tension in sustainable finance is whether ESG initiatives create shareholder value or merely repackage managerial discretion. We propose a conditional theory: sustainability enhances outcomes when governed by dual constraints that bind both strategy and capital. Corporate Venture Capitalists (CVC) bring strategic alignment and access to parent resources, while independent venture capitalists (IVCs) impose exit-driven financial discipline. We formalize this structure in a stylized model with predictable outcomes and use hand-collected data to incorporate the Facebook–Cambridge Analytica scandal as a quasi-exogenous shock to data privacy firms. First, we find CVCs enhance sustainable outcomes in startups. We also find the negative relation between ESG and exit reverses when CVCs and IVCs co-invest. This reversal appears to be driven by industry alignment and greater investor capacity. Results suggest ESG is value-relevant when a dual governance structure simultaneously enforces sustainability goals and market discipline.

AI.tldr: 该研究提出了一个条件性理论：当可持续发展受到战略和资本双重约束时，才能创造价值。企业风险投资(CVC)提供战略协同和母公司资源，而独立风险投资(IVC)施加退出驱动的财务纪律。研究发现，在CVC和IVC共同投资时，ESG与退出的负相关关系会逆转，表明双重治理结构能同时执行可持续发展目标和市场纪律。
AI.research_question: 在什么条件下ESG倡议能够创造股东价值，而不是仅仅代表管理层的自由裁量权？
AI.motivation: 可持续金融中的核心矛盾：ESG倡议是否真正创造股东价值，还是仅仅重新包装了管理层的自由裁量权。
AI.theoretical_framework: 条件性理论：可持续发展在受到战略和资本双重约束时才能增强结果。CVC提供战略协同和母公司资源，IVC施加退出驱动的财务纪律。

AI.practical_contributions: 为投资者提供了关于如何通过CVC和IVC的组合投资来增强ESG价值创造的实践指导。

detail.abstract: This Master’s thesis examines whether and how the COVID-19 pandemic was governed under international law, and to what extent the existing legal mechanisms proved effective in the declaration process. The analysis explores the international legal framework for declaring a pandemic, focusing on the International Health Regulations (IHR) and the role of the World Health Organization (WHO). Despite early evidence of human-to-human transmission, the official recognition of the pandemic occurred with significant delay, raising questions about the interplay between public health imperatives and economic considerations. This thesis therefore investigates the legal procedures and principles guiding the declaration of a pandemic and evaluates how much weight was given to economic protection when making such decisions. The findings are based on a systematic review of legal literature and international policy documents.

Stata-MCP is an independent, open-source project and has no financial, legal, or organizational affiliation with StataCorp LLC, the developer of Stata.

detail.abstract: Data analysis is central to social science research, yet technical barriers still limit efficiency. While Stata lowers the learning cost of coding, further simplification is possible. This study develops Stata-MCP to streamline coding via AI and promote automation in empirical work. Using the ReAct agent framework and a custom evaluation set, we systematically assess LLMs across key stages of empirical research. Results show: (1) LLMs perform well in Stata code generation and debugging; (2) models differ notably in econometric understanding and coding, with the Claude series leading; (3) whether LLMs can conduct empirical analysis independently remains open. We also identify two key technical bottlenecks: (1) improving context management and overcoming window limitations through engineering; (2) fine-tuning the ReAct framework to better align with the needs of social science research.

detail.abstract: As a Black woman with locs, I have personally experienced the impact of hair discrimination throughout my life and career. It has been a constant battle to navigate the societal expectations and racialized notions of professionalism that dictate how my hair should look and conform to Eurocentric standards. It is a topic that is deeply personal to me and one that I believe we need to address to achieve true liberation for all individuals. I embrace and love my natural hair. I spend hours carefully styling my locs, telling stories about their beauty and cultural significance. I wear my hair proudly, knowing it symbolizes my heritage, identity, and individuality. However, as I entered the professional world, I quickly realized that not everyone shared the same appreciation for my locs. During my early years as a lawyer, I faced subtle and not-so-subtle forms of hair discrimination. Colleagues and superiors would make offhand comments about my hair, questioning its cleanliness and professionalism. I would receive sideways glances and whispers as I walked into courtrooms or attended professional events. It became clear that my hair was seen as an obstacle to overcome rather than a beautiful expression of who I am. One particularly memorable incident occurred during professionalism training. As I prepared to ask a question, the speaker made a derisive comment about my locs, insinuating that they made me less competent and less credible, all in the name of “professionalism.” I felt anger rise, but I knew I had to maintain my composure. I responded to her comment gracefully by merely raising an eyebrow. But inside, I was seeing. These experiences, and many others like them, led me to question why some saw my natural hair as unprofessional or inappropriate. Why were locs considered less acceptable than other hairstyles? I knew it did not reflect my abilities as a lawyer or person. The discrimination I faced was based solely on societal norms and racial biases that dictated what was deemed “acceptable” in professional settings. *121 During this time, I became deeply involved in the fight against hair discrimination and advocated for change. I joined organizations and initiatives that sought to challenge the status quo and push for legislation that would protect individuals from hair discrimination. I used my platform as a professor and author to educate others about the impact of hair discrimination on marginalized communities, particularly Black women. Throughout my journey, I have realized that the fight against hair discrimination is not just about hair. It is about dismantling systemic racism and challenging long-held beliefs that perpetuate inequality. It is about redefining what it means to be professional and embracing diversity in all its forms. It is about liberating individuals from the constraints of societal expectations and allowing them to express themselves authentically. I am committed to continuing this important work as an advocate, professor, and author. I will use my voice and platform to raise awareness about the harmful effects of hair discrimination and push for change at every level. I will support and uplift those affected by hair discrimination, providing resources and guidance to help them navigate the challenges they may face. And I will continue to amplify the voices of those fighting for equality and liberation in all areas of life.

The silent hand of central banking: collateral framework In light of the upcoming review of the European Central Bank's monetary policy strategy, this briefing highlights the strategic relevance of a frequently underestimated component of the central banking toolkit: the collateral framework. detail.abstract: This study investigates the public demand for retail Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) and its implications for financial intermediation by focusing on its potential substitution effects on existing digital payment methods and viability as a store of value. Using an information-provision survey experiment, we analyze public responses to technically various CBDC issuance types, including online and offline applications and a physical card type, with and without interest payments. The survey experiment finds that, while CBDC design features do not significantly influence its demand as a payment method, offering positive interest payments can enhance its appeal as a store of value. Moreover, it indicates that payment practices and trust in central banks would have a greater impact on demand for CBDC than its technical design features.

detail.title: We are all Betting (Serving) -Thee Unravelling of Thee Ugly Truth: An Investigative Literature Review
detail.abstract: In the present day world, people involved in betting activities are looked upon with disdain, especially in religious circles. However, an introspection into the terminology used in the betting industry, suggests strong connectedness between betting activities and uplifted societal norms. An example of the present day dilemma is the uplifting of forex and/or crypto traders and the shunning of Aviator pilots (panthers) which are merely uncertified photocopies of traders. In an attempt to clear the mist surrounding this and other misconceptions, this confirmatory study was conducted with an aim to reveal the hidden connectedness of betting activities and acceptable societal norms. To accomplish the main aim of this confirmatory study, inspiration and an investigative non-empirical approach, in the form of literature review were utilised. The literature review process was conducted in accordance to the PRISMA framework. From the findings, it was confirmed, beyond reasonable doubt, that Aviator game and forex/crypto trading are two sides of the same coin. The results also revealed that employment (formalised slavery) and education are essentially betting activities that have been formalised and given official names. Ultimately, it was concluded that having a funeral policy is the only activity that is divergent from betting.

title: Viksit Haryana@2047: A Triad Framework for Inclusive and Sustainable Growth

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicting interests are disclosed by the authors.
declarations.ethicsApproval: None of the authors of this article have undertaken any research with human subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: The authors have no relevant financial or non-financial interests to disclose.

detail.abstract:
Haryana is among the economically advanced states in India. Its past performance and future growth trajectory indicate a strong potential to attain developed economy status in the foreseeable future. This study examines the prospects of Haryana transitioning into a developed economy. The uniqueness of this study lies in the formulation of a comprehensive, three-dimensional framework to assess the state's readiness for this transformation.

A developed economy is typically characterized by high per capita income and a broadly shared high quality of life. Thus, we define a threefold criterion for a developed economy: (1) per capita income exceeding the projected high-income threshold in US dollar; (2) an SDG score of 90 or higher; and (3) an HDI value above 0.85. This comprehensive framework allows for a nuanced assessment of state’s prospects for achieving developed economy status.

To assess the feasibility of this status, we project Haryana’s per capita income in Indian rupee, convert it into US dollar, and compare it with the World Bank’s projected threshold for a High- Income Country (HIC). Thereafter, we evaluate the preparedness of Haryana to attain SDG-2030 score above 90 as a necessary condition, indicating broad-based socio-economic progress and resilience against the middle-income trap. We also employ the Human Development Index (HDI), with a threshold value of 0.85 or above, as a sufficient condition to reflect high human well-being and quality of life.

To project per capita income growth, we apply the Solow Growth Accounting Framework to estimate Haryana’s potential growth at the sectoral level. We also project the future distribution of the workforce across sectors to evaluate per capita growth under different scenarios. However, the real challenge for policymakers lies in translating this potential into reality. Achieving near potential growth will require the proactive adoption of policies that promote geographically and socially inclusive development, alongside a strong emphasis on improving health and education outcomes—including the establishment of globally competitive universities. If these measures are pursued with commitment, Haryana has a credible opportunity to join the ranks of developed economies by the late 2030s—well ahead of India’s national target of 2047.

AI.tldr: 该研究评估了印度哈里亚纳邦向发达经济体转型的前景，提出了一个包含人均收入、SDG得分和HDI指数的三维评估框架，预测该邦有望在2030年代末成为发达经济体。

title: Artificial Identity: How Instructor Race and Gender Influence Student Behavior and Performance in AI-Mediated Learning
affiliations: Yale University - Law School and Yale University - Law School

detail.title: Artificial Identity: How Instructor Race and Gender Influence Student Behavior and Performance in AI-Mediated Learning
detail.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms education, AI-generated instructors offer unprecedented opportunities to scale and personalize learning. Yet, the influence of instructor identity-especially race and gender-remains underexplored in AI-driven contexts. This study provides one of the first randomized controlled experiments examining how instructor identity shapes student engagement, academic performance, and willingness to pay when instructional content is held constant. Leveraging a large-scale field experiment involving over 2,500 students enrolled in an online Coursera course, we randomly assigned students to video instruction with identical content delivered by either a human professor or one of four AI avatars whose appearance varied by race (Black or White) and gender (male or female). The main findings are: First, the avatars were rated similarly to the human professor in teaching effectiveness, and many avatar-instructed students reported that their instructors were likely to be human. There were no significant "man vs. machine" differences in student attrition or grades between the White-male human instructor and the White male avatar. Second, the Black male avatar outperformed the White male avatar with regard to overall course grade (p. = .047), average quiz grade (p. = .099), and number of course items completed (p. = .099). Third, female students that were assigned to female avatars received significantly higher average quiz grades (p. = .042) than those assigned to male avatars.

AI.tldr: 本研究通过随机对照实验发现，在AI生成的教学内容中，教师身份（种族和性别）显著影响学生参与度和学业表现，黑人男性AI教师表现优于白人男性AI教师，女性学生在女性AI教师指导下成绩更好。

AI.method: 大规模随机对照实验，2500多名Coursera在线课程学生被随机分配到人类教授或四种不同种族（黑人/白人）和性别（男/女）的AI虚拟教师组。
AI.findings: 1）AI教师与人类教师教学效果评价相似；2）黑人男性AI教师比白人男性AI教师在课程成绩、测验成绩和完成项目数量上表现更好；3）女性学生在女性AI教师指导下测验成绩显著更高。

title: 'Alive and Well?' Revisiting the Indian Phillips Curve in the Inflation Targeting Era

detail.title: 'Alive and Well?' Revisiting the Indian Phillips Curve in the Inflation Targeting Era
detail.abstract: The empirical existence and structural stability of the Phillips curve in India presents a long-standing macroeconomic puzzle. In this paper, we conduct a critical review of the literature, bifurcating our analysis around the 2016 adoption of the Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework. We first synthesize the foundational debate, contrasting the 'sceptical' literature (Dholakia, 1990) which found no significant inflation-output trade-off, with the 'alive and well' hypothesis (Mazumder, 2011), which posited a conventional, stable relationship. We then analyse the post-FIT literature (including Behera et al., 2018, and Blagrave & Lian, 2020) to examine the empirical evidence for a structural shift. Our synthesis reveals a new consensus: the pre-2016 debate on the curve's existence has been supplanted by a post-2016 debate on its form. We find the contemporary literature indicates a significant 'flattening' of the curve, a shift largely attributed to the anchoring of inflation expectations under the FIT regime. We conclude that the 2016 policy shift was a binding event that fundamentally altered the inflation-output dynamic, rendering pre-2016 stability estimates obsolete for current policy analysis.

AI.tldr: 本文回顾了印度菲利普斯曲线的实证存在性和结构稳定性这一长期宏观经济学谜题。研究发现2016年采用灵活通胀目标制(FIT)框架是一个关键转折点，导致菲利普斯曲线显著平坦化，这主要归因于FIT制度下通胀预期的锚定。

AI.findings: 2016年FIT框架采用导致菲利普斯曲线显著平坦化，通胀预期的锚定是主要原因；前期的存在性争议被后期的形态争议所取代
